mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPI YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy, which reduces borrowing costs and increases liquidity in the market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances where UNRATE decreases & PAYEMS increases MoM.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.25% in a month, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25% MoM.
